title: The Grihya Sutras, Part I: Sânkhâyana and Âsvalâyana
altTitles: Sacred Books of the East, vol. 29
attributionNote: The sutras are ascribed to the teachers Sankhayana and Asvalayana and belong to their Vedic schools. They are school texts, transmitting ritual practice rather than the work of a single author.
description: The Grihya Sutras are the manuals of the householder's ritual: the domestic fire and its daily offerings, the initiation of the student, betrothal and marriage, the birth and naming of children, the first feeding and the tonsure, the offerings to the ancestors, the rules of hospitality and the ceremonies of the seasons. Sankhayana and Asvalayana are the two surviving sutras of the Rigvedic schools, and their texts are the fullest account of the private religion of the Vedic household.
historicalContext: The grihya sutras form one branch of the Kalpa, the Vedic literature of ritual, alongside the srauta sutras for the great public sacrifices. Hermann Oldenberg translated the Sankhayana and Asvalayana texts for the Sacred Books of the East in 1886, with an introduction on the place of domestic ritual in Vedic religion.
availabilityNote: Complete. All four adhyayas of Sankhayana and the four of Asvalayana are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one printed section per chapter. The volume's title page, contents and introduction are not part of the work.
